sentences.text:
Author: Raj Beer Singh
Bench: Raj Beer Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 77
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 3910 of 2023
Applicant :- Savendra
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Mayank Yadav,Vivek Kumar Singh

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
Second supplementary affidavit, filed by the learned counsel for the applicant, is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
This is second bail application on behalf of applicant.
The first bail application of applicant was dismissed for want of prosecution.

The present second bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 239 of 2018,
under Sections 363, 366, 342, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, P.S. Alapur, District Budaun,
with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.

The first information report was lodged against applicant,
Savendra vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141467183/
1 alleging that on 06.03.2018 he has enticed away the minor daughter of informant.

entities.text: Savendra vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was pointed out that in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., victim has stated her age as 18 years and she has stated that on 06.03.2018 she herself has left her home and went to Sakhanu and from there she along with applicant went to Budaun and thereafter to Mumbai and they lived together as husband and wife.

In her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., victim has developed an entirely new story and stated that while she has gone to collect fodder, applicant and co-accused Ravendra and Madan Lal have forcibly dragged her into a vehicle and they have smelt something to her and later on she found herself in Mumbai and that all the said three persons did bad act with her.
Learned counsel pointed out that during investigation involvement of said Ravendra and Madan Lal was found false and charge-sheet was submitted only against applicant/accused.

During trial of applicant/accused,
part statement (examination in chief) of informant and victim girl was recorded and thereafter informant has moved an application under Section 319 Cr.P.C. and consequently the said Ravendra and Madan Lal were summoned by the trial Court under Section 319 Cr.P.C. vide order dated 07.09.2019.

The said co-accused have challenged the said summoning order before this Court by filing an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., wherein by order dated 23.10.2019 proceedings of the case were stayed.

It has been pointed out that since 23.10.2019, the proceedings of the case are continuously lying stayed and thus, no progress has been made in the trial so far, whereas, applicant has already undergone the custody of more than five years.
It was submitted that from above stated facts it is apparent that applicant/accused is confined in jail without trial.

In this connection,
learned counsel has referred the case of Umarmia alias Mamumia vs. State of Gujarat (2017)2 SCC 731, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that an accused has right of speedy trial and that long delay in trial violates the right guaranteed to accused under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Umarmia alias Mamumia vs. State of Gujarat (2017)2 SCC 731
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case the bail was granted to the accused on the basis of period of detention.

Regarding long detention and delay in trial, learned counsel has also referred the case of the Mohd Muslim @
Hussain vs. State (NCT of Delhi), Special Leave Petition (Crl) No. 915 of 2023, Paplu @ Ajay Chauhan vs. State of U.P., [Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 10957 of 2010], decided on 30.03.2012.

entities.text:
Mohd Muslim @
Hussain vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Paplu @ Ajay Chauhan vs. State of U.P., [Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 10957 of 2010]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lastly, it is submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 09.03.2018, having no criminal history and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in trial.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and argued that as per school record, the victim is a minor girl.
However, aforesaid factual position that applicant is in jail since last more than five years and that trial of the case is continuously lying stayed since last four years, could not be disputed.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant Savendra involved in aforesaid case crime, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below subject to following conditions:
1. The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
Savendra vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141467183/
2 2.The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3.The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

entities.text: Savendra vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

5.The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.
